details.description: GPT-4.1 mini is the mid-sized model in OpenAI's GPT-4.1 family, released April 14, 2025 as a smaller, faster alternative to GPT-4.1 built for coding and instruction-following tasks. It takes text and image input and produces text-only output, keeps the family's 1-million-token context window, and has a knowledge cutoff of June 1, 2024. OpenAI reports it matches or beats GPT-4o on several academic and instruction-following benchmarks while cutting latency by nearly half. It is not a reasoning model.
advantages: Scores 87.5% on MMLU and 65.0% on GPQA Diamond, ahead of GPT-4o's 85.7% and 46.0% on the same evaluations (OpenAI's GPT-4.1 announcement).
Scores 84.1% on IFEval and 72.7% on the MMMU vision benchmark, ahead of GPT-4o's 81.0% and 68.7% (OpenAI).
Keeps the GPT-4.1 family's 1-million-token context window despite being the smaller, faster variant (OpenAI API model docs).
Supports function calling, web search, file search, code interpretation and MCP tool use through the Responses API (OpenAI API model docs).
disadvantages: Scores 23.6% on SWE-bench Verified, well below GPT-4o's 33.2% on the same benchmark (OpenAI's GPT-4.1 announcement).
Output is text only; the model does not generate images, audio or video (OpenAI API model docs).
Knowledge cutoff of June 1, 2024 (OpenAI API model docs).
use_cases: Coding assistance and code review at lower cost and latency than full GPT-4.1
Document and image understanding over long, million-token inputs
General-purpose chat and classification where speed and cost matter more than peak accuracy

sources.title: Introducing GPT-4.1 in the API | OpenAI

notes: OpenAI's own GPT-4.1 launch post (openai.com/index/gpt-4-1/) returned HTTP 403 to a direct fetch, so it was read through the r.jina.ai reader proxy; the cited URL is the original OpenAI page whose content was retrieved. OpenAI's API deprecations page does not list gpt-4.1-mini among models scheduled for shutdown, so the catalog's 2027-04-14 deprecation_date fact could not be corroborated or contradicted from primary sources as of this research; only gpt-4.1-nano appears on that page. Benchmark table also lists Aider's polyglot coding (34.7% whole-file) and MultiChallenge (35.8%) for this model, left out of advantages/evaluations as redundant with SWE-bench and IFEval.
